claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately captures the general prohibition in § 91.213(a) that no person may take off an aircraft with inoperative instruments or equipment installed unless the specified conditions are met, subject to the exception in paragraph (d).
Claim C0001 correctly reflects paragraph (a)(1), stating the takeoff condition requiring that an approved Minimum Equipment List exists for the aircraft.

Claim C0002 correctly reflects paragraph (a)(2)'s requirement that the aircraft contain a letter of authorization issued by the responsible Flight Standards office authorizing operation under the MEL.
Claim C0003 accurately reflects the permission in paragraph (a)(2) allowing the letter of authorization to be obtained by written request of the airworthiness certificate holder.
Claim C0004 faithfully reflects the factual provision stating that the Minimum Equipment List and letter of authorization constitute a supplemental type certificate for the aircraft.

Claim C0005 correctly captures the requirements under paragraph (a)(3) that the approved MEL be prepared in accordance with paragraph (b) limitations and provide for operating with instruments and equipment in an inoperable condition.
Claim C0006 accurately states the condition in paragraph (a)(4) that aircraft records available to the pilot must include an entry describing the inoperable instruments and equipment.
Claim C0007 correctly states the condition in paragraph (a)(5) that the aircraft must be operated under all applicable conditions and limitations contained in the MEL and authorization letter.
Claim C0008 accurately consolidates the prohibitions in paragraph (b)(1), (b)(2), and (b)(3) identifying instruments and equipment that may not be included in a Minimum Equipment List.
Claim C0009 accurately reflects paragraph (c), requiring persons authorized to use an approved MEL under subpart K, part 121, 125, or 135 to use that MEL to comply with § 91.213.

unit_judgments.rationale: Unit U0000 is fully covered by claim C0000, preserving the prohibition on takeoff with inoperative instruments/equipment unless conditions are met and the exception for paragraph (d).
Unit U0001 is fully covered by claim C0001, which preserves the condition that an approved MEL exists for the aircraft.
Unit U0002 is fully covered by claim C0002, retaining the condition requiring a letter of authorization issued by Flight Standards within the aircraft.
Unit U0003 is fully covered by claim C0003, maintaining the airworthiness certificate holder's ability to obtain the LOA by written request.
Unit U0004 is fully covered by claim C0004, preserving the legal effect that the MEL and LOA constitute a supplemental type certificate.
Unit U0005 is fully covered by claim C0005, which incorporates the condition that the MEL be prepared in accordance with paragraph (b) limitations.
Unit U0006 is fully covered by claim C0005, which incorporates the condition that the MEL provide for operation with instruments and equipment in an inoperable condition.
Unit U0007 is fully covered by claim C0006, preserving the condition that pilot-available records describe the inoperable instruments and equipment.
Unit U0008 is fully covered by claim C0007, retaining the condition that the aircraft is operated under all applicable MEL and letter conditions and limitations.
Unit U0009 is fully covered within claim C0008, preserving the prohibition against including type certification airworthiness required equipment essential for safe operation in an MEL.
Unit U0010 is fully covered within claim C0008, preserving the prohibition against including AD-required operable equipment in an MEL unless the AD provides otherwise.
Unit U0011 is fully covered within claim C0008, preserving the exclusion of equipment required for specific operations by part 91 from an MEL.
Unit U0012 is fully covered by claim C0009, maintaining the mandate for persons authorized under subpart K, part 121, 125, or 135 to use their approved MEL.
